correctness.rationale: The uniform two-line projector dynamics reduce exactly after the first projection to a Bernoulli stay/switch contraction with q=(1+c²)/2. The residual on either perpendicular line is (1-c²)/2 times squared error. The H eigenvalues are (1±c)/2, yielding the exact worst-initial-error envelope. Differentiating its log gives the cubic h_t; its positive-root uniqueness follows by factorization for t=1, strict derivative sign for t=2 and Descartes for t>=3. h_{t+1}-h_t=2c(1-c²) forces increasing roots, and the root equation proves t(1-c_t)->1 and tG_t(c_t)->1/e. The generalized Rayleigh quotient proves the threshold c=sqrt(2)-1. Executed verify.py: 1,491 rational enumerated cases, 783 rational derivative identities, 500 numeric roots and four long-horizon diagnostics. Finite tests supplement, not substitute for, the analytic quantifier-complete proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact jointly angle-and-initial-error optimized finite-horizon *mean-row residual* and associated cubic/limit/overshoot threshold; it is not the already-known general moment formula or the previously proved general order-1/t Kaczmarz bound. The inspected 2014 general solution-MSE operator representation is an important algebraic precursor, the newer June 2026 result supplies a wider rate theorem, and the May 2026 numerical-stability article studies finite precision rather than this exact-arithmetic residual extremizer. A possible equivalent specialization in other literature remains a residual originality risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent geometry-optimized residual special case may be embedded in older exact MSE or random-projection literature under different terminology.

value.rationale: The finite-horizon condition-number-free residual envelope of the smallest noncommuting Kaczmarz problem has a natural complete optimization and an exact sharp 1/e leading constant, with unique horizon-dependent geometry. The separate first-step threshold c=sqrt(2)-1 shows a principled distinction between Euclidean-error monotonicity and residual-energy monotonicity; it can guide residual monitoring and stress testing. The result is not presented as a universal rate improvement, a textbook renaming or a numerical table recomputation.
